lessons: SCRIPT ROT fixed (CRITICAL): dmey havraa was hardcoded at 418 NIS/day in scripts/salary-calculator.py with the comment frozen since 2023. Kol Zchut, read directly: the private-sector rate was updated on 18.08.2026 to 451.5 NIS for havraa year 2026, nine days before this cycle, and employers who already paid at 418 owe the difference. Fixed in the script, the benefits guide, and a worked table.

WRONG fixed (CRITICAL): the statutory vacation table was wrong on EVERY row and collapsed eleven rows into 7+ years. There are TWO official ladders for a 5-day week. Both are now enumerated in full: expansion-order workplaces (1-5y 12/16, 6-8y 17/23, 9y+ 23/31) and the statutory floor (1-5y 12/16 through 14y+ 20/28). The old table understated a 9-year tech employee by up to 11 net days.

WRONG fixed (CRITICAL): the net-to-bank figure ignored that an employer keren hishtalmut deposit above the 15,712 ceiling is imputed to the employee as taxable income at deposit. The skills own benefits guide said so while the worked example did not use it. On a 40,000 base that is 1,822/month imputed, about 638/month of tax, moving real net from ~23,100 to ~22,450, i.e. below the entire band the skill previously quoted.

WRONG fixed (MAJOR): the skill said employees cannot claim a Section 47 deduction because 47 is scoped to self-employed contributions, then contradicted itself two paragraphs later. Pensuni confirms an additional ceiling exists specifically for salaried employees with unpensioned salary (overtime, shovi rechev, commissions), which is common in tech.

WRONG fixed (MAJOR): the Section 102 embedded-value rule was stated as applying to any grant with value at grant date. 102(b)(3) applies only to an already-traded company or one listing within 90 days, measured on the 30-trading-day pre-grant average. For a private startup the whole benefit can be capital at 25%. This is precisely the distinction that decides a big-tech-versus-startup comparison, which is the skills main use case. Also added two omitted employee-favourable points: the 102 capital track carries no Bituach Leumi or health tax, but does count toward mas yesef.

WRONG fixed (MAJOR): the 14.83% employer stack was presented as what any Israeli contract delivers. The statutory floor is 6.5% + 6% = 12.5%; 8.33% severance is a Section 14 arrangement. Overstated the Israeli side of a foreign-contract comparison by 2.33% of gross.

WRONG fixed (MAJOR): Example 1 said a 38K offer is about 7% below median and quoted a 40-42K band. The skills own data file gives a single 42K median, so the gap is 9.5%. The example also countered at 43K while Step 2 says anchor at the 75th percentile (48K); the departure is now stated and justified rather than silent.

REMOVED (unsourceable): the benefits guide asserted a ~47,465 NIS/month tax-qualifying salary ceiling that corresponds to none of the real 2026 ceilings and could not be traced to any source. Replaced with the four real ceilings, each named: 34,422.5 employer-contribution, 15,712 keren, 9,700 Section 45a, 3,800 severance deposit.

EVIDENCE HYGIENE: pension-tagmulim-severance-2026 cited chamber.org.il (307, unreachable) with a raw_snippet that was author-written summary prose rather than any page quote, i.e. an entry that could never be falsified. Re-pointed to pensuni with a verbatim quote, which is also what proved the 12.5% statutory figure.

RATE-TABLE COMPLETENESS: the BL/health rates are one row of a fifteen-row official employee table. The row is correct for this skills audience, but the reference file now says WHICH row it is and enumerates the rows that differ (controlling shareholder 4.25/11.96, over-70 or disability 3.23/5.17, 67-70 not drawing pension 3.93/10.03, new resident over 62 3.60/7.45, and under-18 or old-age-pension recipients who pay nothing).
SCRIPT BUG fixed: format_nis tested amount >= 1000, so a negative total in --compare mode printed as a bare -227607 with no separators and no NIS suffix. Now tests the magnitude.

DISCLOSURE added: the 900 salary figures have no per-figure provenance and no free authoritative source publishes Israeli tech salary by role, seniority and city. The data file now says so, and says the Q1 2026 snapshot is ageing. The tables are structurally clean (no percentile, seniority or city inversions) but that is not evidence any single number is right.

Deferred: the Israel Tax Authority reference link (gov.il/en/departments/israel_tax_authority) renders an empty SPA shell and is cited as the source for brackets, credit points AND Section 102, none of which could be read there. Replace with the ITA computation aid next cycle.

Deferred: the benefits guide describes contributing 8.33% to severance as being Section 14, but Section 14 requires a written arrangement under the General Approval; the rate alone does not create it, and the guides own Red Flags section treats them as separate.
Deferred: the keren employer exemption is also capped at 3x the employee contribution, so a 7.5/2.5 split sits exactly at the limit and an employee-side reduction silently breaks it. Not yet stated.

OVER-CORRECTED, then corrected again (the Judge caught me): my Section 47 fix said the deduction is open to salaried employees, full stop. Pensuni, read directly: mi she-scharo ha-mevutach oleh be-2026 al 24,250 lo yihye zakai le-nikuy. Above 24,250 insured salary, which is essentially this skills whole audience, there is NO Section 47 deduction, only a 45a credit at 5% of the unpensioned income capped at 9,700. The original text was wrong and my first fix was wrong in the opposite direction. Now stated as a two-row table keyed on insured salary. This is the remediation-reintroduces-the-defect pattern.

REVIEWER WAS WRONG, verified against the source: the Expert argued the two vacation ladders are internally impossible because the expansion-order ladder gives 23 net days at 9 years while the statutory ladder tops out at 20 at 14 years. An expansion order may lawfully exceed the statutory floor, and Kol Zchut states explicitly that where both could apply the employee gets the HIGHER of the two. The Experts reasoning was wrong; its actionable point was right, because I had written most of the tech sector with no support. Now the order is named and its exclusions are listed (fewer than four employees, government and municipal companies, workplaces where the 5-day week is set by collective agreement, employers excluded by the supervisory committee).

LEGAL GATE: Tier B, notice added. The fresh-context legal-review gate rejected the Experts reserved-act argument (Chok Roei Cheshbon reserves audit and attestation and expressly excludes bookkeeping; the tax-advisers law reserves REPRESENTATION before the authority, and this skill files nothing) but upheld it on the specificity axis: Steps 3.5, 3.6 and 4 reach concrete conclusions about the users own facts, which is S2 x F1 = Tier B. The TIER_A_TAX notice now sits immediately after the H1 in both files and a legal clause opens all four description surfaces. The finding was INHERITED: the pristine v1.4.0 copy fails verify_legal identically.

Fixed (Expert MAJOR): the 12.5-versus-14.83 correction had landed only in the Gotcha. The guides Section 1 summary, its Section 14 framing and its Red Flags list all still hardcoded 8.33%, and the Red Flags list called the statutory-compliant 6% a red flag. Section 14 is now described as a written arrangement rather than a contribution rate, and both sides of signing it are stated for the first time.

Fixed (Expert MAJOR): Example 3 told the user to upgrade a pension that was already at the statutory floor and claimed the upgrade adds about 40K/year. Recomputed from the skills own salary table: employer keren at 7.5% on the Haifa mid DevOps median of 31K is 27,900/year. The 30-50K band had the same problem at its top.

Flagged, not yet fixed (Expert CRITICAL, deferred with reasons): the company-car grade table reflects the pre-2010 price-group method; vehicles registered from 01.01.2010 use a linear formula on list price. The Cibus/10bis row said tax-exempt, which is probably inverted for off-premises meal cards. The meal row now says taxable in most configurations, verify before valuing, and the grade table is flagged, but the correct valuation method has NOT been written and needs a Tax Authority source next cycle.

Deferred (Expert CRITICAL, sized too large for this cycle): unvested and vested-unexercised 102 equity on leaving (forfeiture, the post-termination exercise window, and losing capital treatment by disposing inside 24 months) is absent, in a skill whose core scenario is changing employer. Also absent: Israeli tax-residency and self-reporting exposure on a foreign-remote contract, which is currently modelled only as a lost-benefits shortfall.

Deferred (Expert MAJOR): the script applies no ceilings at all (keren 15,712, pension 34,422.5, BL 51,910), has no brackets, no 45a and no BL tier, so it cannot reproduce any figure in gross-to-net-2026.md, yet Step 3 tells the user to run it. Its pre-tax effective pay of 36,600 on a 40K base will be read as take-home against a real 22,450. Also: signing_bonus is added to total_annual_compensation as if recurring, and an employer-NI comment of ~4.51% matches no published employer rate.

Deferred (Expert MAJOR): the keren imputation was taxed at the 35% marginal rate only; the same imputed amount also attracts the 12.17% employee NI and health tier, about 222/month more, so the corrected 22,450 is still slightly optimistic.

Deferred (Expert MAJOR/MINOR): pension fund versus bituach menahalim versus kupat gemel is three bullets and mislabels a comprehensive pension fund as a kupat gemel; 30-day post-termination pension continuity is absent; signing-bonus tax treatment and clawback are absent; the 3,800 severance-deposit ceiling has no denominator stated.

STALE fixed (verified directly against btl.gov.il): the NI/health reduced-rate threshold was the 2025 value of 7,522 (shekels) but the 2026 figure is 7,703 (effective 01.01.2026), and the contribution ceiling was the 2025 figure of 50,695 but is 51,910 in 2026. Fixed in SKILL.md, SKILL_HE.md, and gross-to-net-2026.md, and recalculated the worked examples (NI/health charge ~4,259.4, net-to-bank ~23,101.1). The rates (1.04%/7%, 3.23%/5.17%) are unchanged; only the threshold/ceiling move with the average wage each year.
WRONG fixed: keren hishtalmut tax-benefited salary ceiling was stated as 15,751 (a digit transposition) but is 15,712 NIS/month (the doc's own correct 1,571 deposit figure proves it). Fixed.

MAJOR added: keren above-ceiling tax treatment for high earners (employer contribution above 15,712 is taxable income AND the growth on that portion loses the after-6-years CGT exemption), a real point for 40K+ salaries; and a 2026 soft-market leverage caveat in Step 5 (layoffs / repriced equity mean weaker candidate leverage than the 2021-2022 peak; do not coach an aggressive counter when the candidate has no alternative).

Verified CORRECT (no change): the April 2026 income-tax bracket revision (20% widened to 19,000, 31% 19,001-25,100) and credit point 242 NIS, Section 102 (25% / 24-month / RSU grant-date value = ordinary income), Section 45a (35%, 679/mo, 9,700 ceiling, ~2,852/yr), pension 6.5%+8.33%=14.83% with Section 14, dmei havraah 418 NIS, and the salary benchmarks (align with 2026 levels.fyi Israel).

Fixed MINOR: reworded the pension disability framing to the accurate 5%-tagmulim-floor / 7.5%-combined-cap rule; noted in salary-calculator.py that the employer-cost total excludes employer-side National Insurance.

CRITICAL fixed (Expert round 2): the keren 'max tax-benefited employer deposit: 1,571 at 10%' mislabeled the COMBINED employer+employee 10% deposit as the employer's. The employer (7.5%) tax-benefited deposit at the 15,712 ceiling is 1,178 NIS/month; clarified both (employer 1,178 at 7.5%, combined 1,571 at 10%).

MAJOR fixed (Expert round 2): the salary-calculator.py employer-NI note used the stale 2025 reduced rate (3.55 percent) and wrongly attributed health tax to the employer. Corrected to the 2026 employer NI of ~4.51% reduced / 7.6% full, and clarified the employer pays NI only (health tax is employee-side).
Decoded all percent-encoded Hebrew source URLs to literal Hebrew (the verify-evidence gate read %94/%95/%9X byte pairs as phantom 9X% percentages, the known false-positive).

Deferred (MINOR): dmei havraah may rise to ~451.5 if the pending extension order is signed (update both files if so); add ESPP lookback mechanics, sign-on/retention clawback clauses, and RSU double-trigger (liquidity-event) vesting for late-stage startup offers.
